# live/ — value-free response skeletons captured from the sandbox

**These files are not documentation fixtures.** Everything else under
`conformance/testdata/` is a *minimal instance of a published OpenAPI schema*,
generated by `tools/conformance/gen_fixtures.py` from Webull's own reference
pages and read by `conformance.CompareBody`. The files in this directory are
the *shape of what the sandbox actually answered*, captured by
`examples/live-probe -capture` from a running server. Different author,
different input, different consumer, and a reader who confuses the two would
read a live observation as a published promise.

Two properties make that confusion harmless even if you do it:

1. **There is no value here.** Every leaf is a placeholder that stands for a
   kind and nothing else — a JSON string becomes `"1"`, a number becomes `-1`,
   a boolean becomes `true`, a `null` stays `null`. Every member name the
   sandbox sent is kept, because a name the SDK does not carry is one of the two
   things this harness exists to find. So a file here is a list of names and a
   list of kinds: no price, no size, no timestamp, no account id, no symbol, and
   nothing to recover. `conformance.TestLiveSkeletonsCarryNoValue` walks every
   committed file and fails on any leaf that is not a placeholder.
2. **A skeleton is indented, a documentation fixture is not.** The fixtures
   beside this directory are one compact line; these are one-space indented and
   sorted by member name, so the same body always produces the same bytes and a
   diff after a re-run means the sandbox sent something different.

## What is here

One file per endpoint, named exactly as its documentation fixture is named, under
the `live/` prefix: `trading/GET-trading-orders-get.json` here is
`trading/GET-trading-orders-get.json` in `manifest.json`. The two trees join row
for row on the name.

`../live-manifest.json` is the index: for each file, the SDK symbol that
produced it, the HTTP status the capture call was answered with, the host, the
clock reading, and whether the live body unmarshalled into the SDK's own
response type. Only endpoints the reachability census recorded as **HTTP 200**
are captured. A 404, 403, 417, 500 or 504 is a live answer about whether an
endpoint is served, but its body is Webull's error shape, and reducing one would
compare an error against a documented success response.

Nothing in this directory is written by hand and nothing here is edited by hand.
Both trees are generated, and regenerating either is a diff a reviewer reads.

## One caveat about the line endings

`skeletonBytes` in the manifest is the length the probe wrote, in LF. This
repository's `.gitattributes` is `* text=auto`, so a checkout with
`core.autocrlf=true` — `windows-latest` among them — materialises these files
with CRLF and they are one byte longer per line there. That is a line-ending
policy, not a content change, and it is why no test asserts a byte length
against the committed tree the way the documentation fixtures do.
